provenance.citation: Konieczny, S., & Pino Pérez, R. (2002). Merging Information Under Constraints: A Logical Framework. Journal of Logic and Computation, 12(5), 773–808.
provenance.locus: Sections 5–6: the Σ (sum) family is majoritarian, the GMax (leximax) family is egalitarian (arbitration); the two operator families are distinguished exactly by profiles where a repeated majority base opposes a single dissenting base.
provenance.notes: Canonical discriminating profile over atoms {p,q}: E = {K1 = p∧q, K2 = p∧q, K3 = ¬p∧¬q}, IC = ⊤, Dalal distance. Hand-computed distance vectors: world (p,q): (0,0,2) → Σ=2, GMax-sorted (2,0,0); worlds (p,¬q)/(¬p,q): (1,1,1) → Σ=3, GMax (1,1,1); world (¬p,¬q): (2,2,0) → Σ=4, GMax (2,2,0). Σ selects the majority world (p,q); GMax selects the egalitarian pair {(p,¬q),(¬p,q)} since (1,1,1) <_lex (2,0,0). This Σ-vs-GMax disagreement is the paper's stated behavioural difference between the two families.

input.intent: merge the conflicting profile under Sigma aggregation

input_gmax.intent: merge the conflicting profile under GMax aggregation

expected.notes: Σ is majoritarian, GMax is egalitarian — the operators disagree on this profile (Konieczny & Pino Pérez 2002).
